evals.prompt: Here's the spec: add password reset via email — user requests a reset link, clicks a tokenized link, and sets a new password. Write an implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: Restates the goal and success criteria, then decomposes into small dependency-ordered phases (e.g. token model + request endpoint -> email send -> reset endpoint + validation). Every task says what to change, where, and how to verify (a test or observable behavior). Lists risks (token expiry/entropy, single-use, rate limiting), assumptions, and out-of-scope. Does not write the implementation code. Writes the plan to docs/plans/.
assertions: Decomposes into small phases ordered by dependency, each independently verifiable
Every task states what to change, where, and how to verify it (test or observable behavior)
Lists risks/assumptions and an explicit out-of-scope section
Does NOT write the implementation code

evals.expected_output: Recognizes the ask is too vague to plan (no requirements, no success criteria, unknown data/audience) and STOPS to clarify scope and requirements rather than inventing a plan. Asks for the design/requirements to be nailed down first.
assertions: Recognizes the spec is too vague/under-specified to plan
STOPS and asks for scope/requirements/success criteria instead of inventing a plan
Does not fabricate a detailed plan from nothing

evals.prompt: Plan a URL shortener, and make it future-proof for analytics, teams, custom domains, and billing we might add later.
evals.expected_output: Plans only the minimal current requirement (create short link, redirect) in small verifiable phases, and moves analytics/teams/custom-domains/billing to an explicit Out of scope (YAGNI) section rather than planning speculative future work. Each task has a verification step.
assertions: Plans the minimal current requirement (shorten + redirect), not the speculative extras
Moves analytics/teams/custom-domains/billing to an explicit out-of-scope (YAGNI) section
Each task still has a concrete verification step

evals.prompt: We need to add rate limiting to the POST /login endpoint. Plan it.
evals.expected_output: Grounds the plan by reading the existing login endpoint/middleware first, then produces small ordered phases each with a verification (e.g. a test asserting the Nth request is throttled), and notes risks (locking out legitimate users, shared-IP/NAT, distributed counters). Marks a review gate before shipping. Does not implement it.
assertions: Says to read the existing endpoint/middleware/code before planning
Produces small ordered phases each with a concrete verification step
Notes risks such as false-positive lockout or shared-IP/distributed-counter concerns
